meta.name: Card Dispute Reason-Code Knowledge Base
meta.notes: Resolution steps are written for a card-issuer / merchant dispute analyst. time_limit_days is the representative cardholder filing window for the network; always confirm against the current network rulebook and regional overrides.

fields.applies_when: signals in the case that point to this code
fields.does_not_apply_when: look-alike situations and the code to use instead
fields.required_evidence: what the cardholder / issuer needs to progress the claim
fields.resolution_steps: ordered actions to work and resolve the dispute
fields.merchant_remedy: how the merchant can pre-empt or overturn the chargeback
fields.time_limit_days: representative filing window in calendar days
fields.prevention: how to stop this dispute type recurring

codes.label: EMV Liability Shift Counterfeit Fraud
codes.summary: Counterfeit chip card used at a chip-capable terminal that did not read the chip.
codes.definition: Card-present sale the cardholder denies, where the card was a counterfeit EMV card and the transaction was swiped, key-entered, or sent with incomplete chip data instead of a full chip read.
applies_when: Card-present transaction denied by cardholder
Genuine card was not used - counterfeit/cloned card
Terminal was chip-capable but fell back to magstripe or key-entry
Chip data in the authorization message was absent or incomplete
does_not_apply_when: The real card was lost or stolen - use VISA-10.2
No EMV liability-shift mechanics apply (keyed, unattended, contactless) - use VISA-10.3
Card was not physically present - use VISA-10.4
required_evidence: Authorization and clearing records showing POS entry mode
Confirmation the genuine card was in the cardholder's possession
resolution_steps: Confirm the transaction is card-present and the cardholder denies it.
Pull the authorization record and check POS entry mode / chip data presence.
Verify the genuine card was not used (cardholder still holds it).
If the terminal was chip-capable but no full chip read occurred, liability sits with the acquirer/merchant - raise the chargeback under 10.1.
Send the pre-arbitration / chargeback with the entry-mode evidence attached.
Diarise the representment window and review any merchant rebuttal for a valid chip-read proof.
merchant_remedy: Provide proof of a successful chip read (TVR/TSI, cryptogram) or a PIN-verified CVM
Show the card was on the Card Recovery Bulletin exception or under floor limit
codes.prevention: Keep EMV terminals in chip-first mode; do not train staff to swipe on chip errors; disable key-entry fallback where possible.

codes.label: EMV Liability Shift Lost/Stolen
codes.summary: Real lost/stolen card used at a terminal that should have forced PIN but did not.
codes.definition: Card-present fraud using a genuine card that was lost, stolen or never received, at a POS that was not PIN-compliant or let a chip transaction complete without PIN.
applies_when: Genuine (not counterfeit) card used without authority
Card reported lost / stolen / never received
Terminal lacked PIN capability or completed chip online without PIN
does_not_apply_when: Card was counterfeit - use VISA-10.1
Generic card-present fraud with no PIN liability-shift failure - use VISA-10.3
Card-absent transaction - use VISA-10.4
required_evidence: Authorization record showing CVM used (PIN vs none)
resolution_steps: Confirm card-present and that the card was genuine but lost/stolen.
Check the CVM in the authorization data - was PIN required and performed?
If a PIN-preferring card completed without PIN at a capable terminal, raise 10.2.
Attach the lost/stolen report and CVM evidence to the chargeback.
Track the representment window; accept only a valid PIN-verification rebuttal.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of successful online PIN or offline PIN verification
Proof the CVM was correctly cardholder-signature per card configuration
codes.prevention: Deploy PIN-capable terminals; ensure chip transactions enforce the card's preferred CVM.

codes.label: Other Fraud - Card Present Environment
codes.summary: Card-present fraud that is not a counterfeit or lost/stolen EMV liability-shift case.
codes.definition: Catch-all for card-present unauthorized transactions once 10.1 and 10.2 are ruled out - e.g. manually keyed sales, unattended terminals, or contactless taps with no chip-fallback dispute.
applies_when: Card-present, cardholder denies the sale
No counterfeit and no lost/stolen EMV mechanics in play
Keyed / unattended / contactless acceptance
does_not_apply_when: Counterfeit chip card - VISA-10.1
Lost/stolen with PIN failure - VISA-10.2
Card not present - VISA-10.4
resolution_steps: Rule out 10.1 (counterfeit) and 10.2 (lost/stolen PIN failure).
Confirm the transaction was genuinely card-present.
Raise 10.3 with the cardholder denial and entry-mode data.
Assess merchant compelling-evidence rebuttal (prior undisputed history, delivery to cardholder address).
Escalate to pre-arbitration if the rebuttal does not meet Visa's compelling-evidence bar.
merchant_remedy: Visa compelling evidence: signed receipt, matching AVS, prior transaction history with same card/device
codes.prevention: Avoid manual key-entry; secure unattended terminals; capture cardholder verification at point of sale.

codes.label: Other Fraud - Card Absent Environment
codes.summary: E-commerce / phone / mail order transaction the cardholder says they never authorised.
codes.definition: Card-absent (online, MOTO, recurring) transaction disputed as unauthorised, where 3-D Secure liability did not shift to the issuer.
applies_when: Channel is ecommerce / phone_order / mail_order / recurring
Cardholder denies making or authorising the purchase
No successful 3-D Secure authentication protecting the merchant
does_not_apply_when: Card-present fraud - use VISA-10.1/10.2/10.3
Cardholder recognises the merchant but disputes goods/service - use a 13.x code
Transaction was 3-D Secure authenticated - issuer may hold liability
required_evidence: Merchant name, descriptor and transaction channel
AVS/CVV2 and 3-D Secure result from the authorization
resolution_steps: Confirm the channel is card-absent and the cardholder denies the purchase.
Check whether 3-D Secure (EMV 3DS) authentication succeeded - if it did, liability may sit with the issuer, not the merchant.
Screen for 'friendly fraud' - look for prior orders, same device, delivery to the cardholder's address.
If merchant is liable, raise 10.4 with the denial and authorization data.
Review any merchant compelling-evidence package (proof of digital delivery, IP/device match, prior use).
Progress to pre-arbitration if evidence is insufficient.
merchant_remedy: Proof of 3-D Secure authentication
Compelling evidence: delivery confirmation to cardholder address, device/IP fingerprint match, account login history, prior undisputed purchases
codes.prevention: Enable 3-D Secure, AVS and CVV2 checks; use device fingerprinting and velocity rules on high-risk orders.

codes.label: Visa Fraud Monitoring Program
codes.summary: Chargeback generated because the merchant is in a Visa fraud-monitoring programme.
codes.definition: Issued when a transaction is identified through the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program (VFMP) because the merchant's fraud levels breached programme thresholds - independent of a single cardholder claim.
applies_when: Case references VFMP / fraud-monitoring identification
Merchant fraud-to-sales ratio exceeded programme thresholds
No standard cardholder dispute narrative required
does_not_apply_when: An ordinary single-transaction fraud claim - use 10.3 or 10.4
Dispute is about goods/services - use 13.x
required_evidence: Transaction record matching the flagged merchant and period
resolution_steps: Confirm the transaction was flagged under VFMP, not by a cardholder.
Match the transaction to the VFMP reporting period and merchant identifier.
Raise 10.5 - note representment rights are limited for VFMP items.
Log for merchant-monitoring MIS; feed back to acquirer risk team.
merchant_remedy: Very limited - representment only where the transaction was not actually reported under VFMP or was already refunded
codes.prevention: Merchant must exit the monitoring programme by reducing fraud ratio (3DS, screening, blocking high-risk BINs/geographies).

codes.label: Card Recovery Bulletin
codes.summary: Transaction completed on a card listed on the Card Recovery Bulletin without authorization.
codes.definition: Merchant completed a transaction without authorization on an account that was listed on the Card Recovery Bulletin / Exception File at the time.
applies_when: No authorization obtained (or below-floor-limit assumed)
Account was on the Card Recovery Bulletin / exception file
Transaction date falls within the listing period
does_not_apply_when: Authorization was attempted and declined - use VISA-11.2
No authorization at all and card not on the bulletin - use VISA-11.3
required_evidence: Proof the account was on the CRB for the transaction date
Authorization log showing no approval code
resolution_steps: Verify there is no valid authorization approval for the transaction.
Confirm the account appeared on the Card Recovery Bulletin on the transaction date.
Raise 11.1 citing the CRB listing.
Reject any merchant rebuttal that lacks a valid authorization code.
merchant_remedy: Provide a valid authorization approval code obtained at or after the transaction time
codes.prevention: Always seek electronic authorization; never rely on floor limits for chip/online-capable terminals.

codes.label: Declined Authorization
codes.summary: Merchant went ahead after the authorization request was declined.
codes.definition: The authorization request was declined (or referred and not completed) yet the merchant still submitted the transaction for clearing.
applies_when: Authorization response was 'decline' / 'pick up' / 'refer to issuer'
Transaction was still cleared and posted
Cardholder or issuer disputes the resulting charge
does_not_apply_when: Authorization was simply never requested - use VISA-11.3
Card was on the recovery bulletin - use VISA-11.1
required_evidence: Authorization log showing the decline response code and time
Clearing record for the same transaction
resolution_steps: Retrieve the authorization history for the card and amount.
Confirm a decline response preceded the clearing submission.
Raise 11.2 with the decline record.
Only accept a representment that shows a later successful authorization for the same transaction.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of a subsequent approved authorization for the identical transaction
codes.prevention: Configure the POS/gateway to block settlement of declined authorizations; do not re-attempt manually.

codes.label: No Authorization / Late Presentment
codes.summary: Transaction cleared with no authorization ever obtained, OR presented for clearing after the allowed time window.
codes.definition: The merchant did not obtain authorization for a transaction that required it, and the cardholder or issuer disputes the charge. Effective 13 Apr 2024 Visa retired the separate 12.1 (Late Presentment) code and folded that scenario into 11.3 as well, so this code now also covers a transaction presented for settlement outside the permitted window from the transaction date.
applies_when: No authorization request on record for the transaction
Transaction value was above any applicable floor limit
Charge posted and is disputed
Gap between transaction date and processing/clearing date exceeds the network window (late presentment)
does_not_apply_when: Authorization was requested and declined - use VISA-11.2
Card was on the recovery bulletin - use VISA-11.1
Amount exceeded the approved amount only - consider a processing-error code
required_evidence: Authorization system search showing no request/approval
Transaction date vs clearing date from the settlement record, for late-presentment claims
resolution_steps: Search the authorization records for any approval tied to the PAN, amount and date.
Confirm none exists and the transaction required authorization, OR compare transaction date to clearing date if the claim is about delay.
Raise 11.3 (No Authorization / Late Presentment).
Reconcile against 11.1/11.2 to make sure the more specific code does not apply.
Reject rebuttals without a valid approval code (or, for late presentment, without proof the transaction was presented within the allowed window).
merchant_remedy: Produce a valid authorization approval code covering the full cleared amount, or proof the transaction was presented within the allowed window
codes.prevention: Authorize every transaction electronically; reconcile settlement files against approvals daily; settle promptly, don't hold transactions.

codes.label: Late Presentment (RETIRED 13 Apr 2024 - use VISA-11.3)
codes.deprecated_note: Visa retired this code effective 13 April 2024 and folded late presentment into VISA-11.3, now labelled 'No Authorization / Late Presentment'. Kept in this KB only because the ML classifier and SLM in this project were trained before the retirement and may still emit VISA-12.1 for a late-presentment case - treat any such result as VISA-11.3 under the current Visa rulebook, and route new training data to VISA-11.3 instead.
codes.summary: RETIRED - Transaction submitted for clearing after the allowed time window. Use VISA-11.3 instead.
codes.definition: The merchant presented the transaction for settlement outside the permitted number of days from the transaction date, and the account is now closed, over-limit, or the delay caused the dispute. As of 13 Apr 2024 this is filed under VISA-11.3, not a standalone 12.1.
applies_when: Gap between transaction date and processing/clearing date exceeds the network window
Account since closed or unable to be charged back through normal means
does_not_apply_when: The amount or currency is wrong - use 12.5 / 12.3
It is a duplicate - use 12.6
Goods/services dispute - use 13.x
Current Visa rulebook: this scenario is now VISA-11.3, not 12.1
required_evidence: Transaction date vs clearing date from the settlement record
Statement showing when the charge posted
resolution_steps: Compare the transaction date with the settlement/clearing date.
Confirm the delay exceeds the applicable presentment window.
Raise 12.1 (Late Presentment) with both dates evidenced.
Check whether the cardholder still recognises and accepts the underlying purchase - if so the recovery may be limited to loss caused by the delay.
merchant_remedy: Show the transaction was in fact presented within the allowed window
Show the cardholder account was open and in good standing when presented
codes.prevention: Settle daily; never hold authorizations open for extended periods; capture on shipment within policy.

codes.label: Incorrect Transaction Code
codes.summary: Transaction cleared with the wrong transaction type / code (e.g. debit vs credit).
codes.definition: The transaction was processed with an incorrect transaction code or type indicator, causing it to post incorrectly to the cardholder's account.
applies_when: Transaction type indicator is wrong (sale vs refund, debit vs credit)
Posting direction or category on the statement is incorrect
does_not_apply_when: A credit was posted as a charge specifically - Amex uses AM-P03; for Visa still 12.2/13.6 depending on facts
Amount is wrong - use 12.5
required_evidence: Clearing record showing the code actually used
resolution_steps: Identify the transaction code intended vs the code submitted.
Confirm the mis-code caused the incorrect posting.
Raise 12.2 with the receipt and clearing record.
Request the merchant reprocess correctly and refund the incorrect entry.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the transaction code was correct and posted as intended
codes.prevention: Validate transaction-type flags in the gateway; reconcile refunds vs sales in daily settlement.

codes.label: Incorrect Currency
codes.summary: Cardholder was charged in, or converted to, the wrong currency - or DCC rules were broken.
codes.definition: The transaction currency presented differs from the currency in which the cardholder agreed to transact, or Dynamic Currency Conversion was applied without proper cardholder choice/disclosure.
applies_when: Currency billed differs from the currency on the receipt / agreed at POS
DCC applied without the cardholder actively choosing it
Exchange applied that the cardholder did not consent to
does_not_apply_when: Only the amount is wrong, currency is right - use 12.5
Cardholder simply dislikes their bank's FX rate on a correctly-billed foreign transaction
resolution_steps: Compare the agreed transaction currency with the currency actually cleared.
If DCC was used, check for evidence the cardholder was offered a choice and accepted.
Raise 12.3 with the receipt and statement.
Seek re-presentment of the transaction in the correct currency.
merchant_remedy: Receipt/terminal log showing the cardholder chose DCC and the billed currency matches that choice
codes.prevention: Configure terminals so DCC is a genuine cardholder choice with clear rate disclosure; bill in the local currency by default.

codes.label: Incorrect Account Number
codes.summary: Transaction posted to an account number that does not match the card used.
codes.definition: The account number in the clearing record does not match the account number of the card actually presented, so the wrong cardholder was charged.
applies_when: PAN on the statement differs from the card the cardholder used / holds
Key-entry or tokenisation error produced a mismatched PAN
Cardholder does not hold an account matching the transaction
does_not_apply_when: Cardholder recognises the account but disputes the purchase - use a fraud or 13.x code
Amount is wrong - use 12.5
required_evidence: Card / account details held by the cardholder
Any merchant receipt showing the entered number
resolution_steps: Confirm the PAN in the clearing record is not the cardholder's.
Check for a transposition / key-entry error at the merchant.
Raise 12.4 (Incorrect Account Number).
Have the merchant reverse and re-key to the correct account.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the PAN cleared matches the card actually presented (imprint, chip data, tokenisation record)
codes.prevention: Avoid manual PAN entry; use chip/contactless/tokenised capture; validate with Luhn and BIN checks.

codes.label: Incorrect Amount
codes.summary: Cleared amount is not the amount the cardholder agreed to.
codes.definition: The transaction amount posted differs from the amount authorised or agreed at the point of sale (transposition, tip error, wrong keying, partial-shipment mismatch).
applies_when: Statement amount != receipt / agreed amount
Authorised amount and settled amount differ beyond tolerance
Tip or surcharge added that the cardholder did not agree
does_not_apply_when: Currency is the problem - use 12.3
Duplicate charge - use 12.6
Amount is right but goods are faulty - use 13.3
required_evidence: Itemised receipt / order confirmation with the agreed amount
Statement entry with the cleared amount
resolution_steps: Obtain the agreed amount (receipt, quote, order confirmation).
Compare with the authorised and settled amounts.
Raise 12.5 for the difference (or the full amount if unquantifiable).
Ask the merchant to refund the overcharge; represent only with a signed authority for the higher amount.
merchant_remedy: Signed receipt or agreement showing the cardholder authorised the exact amount cleared (including tip/surcharge)
codes.prevention: Confirm the final amount with the cardholder before capture; control tip-adjustment windows; reconcile auth vs settle.

codes.label: Duplicate Processing/Paid by Other Means
codes.summary: Same purchase charged twice, or already paid by another method.
codes.definition: A single purchase was processed more than once to the same card, or the cardholder already settled it by cash, cheque, another card or other means.
applies_when: Two or more identical charges (merchant, amount, date) on the card
Cardholder holds a separate receipt proving payment by another method
does_not_apply_when: Charges are for genuinely separate purchases
Amount differs because of legitimate additional items - use 12.5
required_evidence: Both/all transaction entries from the statement
Proof of the alternative payment (cash receipt, other card statement)
resolution_steps: Identify the duplicate entries or the alternative payment proof.
Confirm they relate to one and the same purchase.
Raise 12.6 for the duplicate/second payment.
Reject representment unless the merchant proves two distinct goods/services were provided.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of two separate orders / deliveries, or that the 'other means' payment was refunded
codes.prevention: De-duplicate on order ID at the gateway; void rather than re-run failed captures; reconcile multi-tender transactions.

codes.label: Invalid Data
codes.summary: Authorization contained invalid or missing data required by Visa rules.
codes.definition: The transaction was authorised or cleared with invalid, inconsistent or missing mandatory data elements, breaching Visa processing requirements.
applies_when: Mandatory data elements missing/invalid (MCC, entry mode, indicators)
Authorization data does not reconcile with clearing data
does_not_apply_when: The specific error is a wrong amount/currency/account - use 12.5 / 12.3 / 12.4
It is a late presentment - use 12.1
required_evidence: Authorization and clearing records showing the invalid/missing field
Reference to the Visa rule breached
resolution_steps: Compare authorization and clearing messages field-by-field.
Identify the invalid or missing mandatory element.
Raise 12.7 citing the specific data breach.
Feed back to the acquirer for merchant processing remediation.
merchant_remedy: Corrected records showing the data element was valid and present
codes.prevention: Certify gateway/processor message formatting; monitor authorization/clearing match rates.

codes.label: Merchandise/Services Not Received
codes.summary: Cardholder paid but never received the goods or services.
codes.definition: The cardholder was billed for merchandise or services that were not received by the expected delivery/performance date, or the merchant was unable/unwilling to provide them.
applies_when: Expected delivery or service date has passed with no delivery/performance
Merchant ceased trading before delivering
Goods still 'in transit' well beyond the promised date
does_not_apply_when: Goods arrived but are wrong/defective - use 13.3
Cardholder cancelled the order - use 13.7
A promised refund was not paid - use 13.6
required_evidence: Order confirmation with expected delivery/performance date
Proof the cardholder contacted the merchant (date, outcome)
Statement that goods/services were not received
resolution_steps: Confirm the agreed delivery / service date has passed.
Check the cardholder attempted to resolve with the merchant first (network requirement).
Verify the merchant has no delivery confirmation.
Raise 13.1 with the order confirmation and merchant-contact evidence.
Assess any merchant proof of delivery / performance before accepting representment.
merchant_remedy: Signed proof of delivery / collection, tracking to the cardholder's address, or evidence services were rendered
codes.prevention: Publish realistic delivery dates; use tracked delivery with signature for higher-value orders; proactively refund undeliverable orders.

codes.label: Cancelled Recurring Transaction
codes.summary: Recurring / subscription charge continued after the cardholder cancelled.
codes.definition: The merchant billed a recurring transaction after the cardholder cancelled the agreement or after the issuer notified the merchant to stop (e.g. via Visa Account Updater / stop instruction).
applies_when: Cardholder cancelled the subscription/membership before the billing date
Merchant charged again after a valid cancellation
Cardholder revoked authority in writing
does_not_apply_when: Cardholder never cancelled, just forgot - not a valid dispute
One-off purchase, not recurring - use 13.1 / 13.3
Free-trial-to-paid conversion misrepresented - consider 13.5
required_evidence: Date and method of cancellation and any confirmation reference
Terms showing how cancellation is made
resolution_steps: Obtain proof of cancellation (email, portal screenshot, confirmation number) and its date.
Confirm the disputed charge is dated after the cancellation took effect.
Raise 13.2 for the post-cancellation billing.
Block future authorizations from that merchant / set up a stop.
Review merchant rebuttal for evidence the cancellation was invalid or later.
merchant_remedy: Evidence no cancellation was received, or that it was received after the disputed billing cycle cut-off
codes.prevention: Honour cancellations immediately; send cancellation confirmations; support Visa Account Updater and stop-payment instructions.

codes.label: Not As Described or Defective Merchandise/Services
codes.summary: Goods or services received but materially different from description, or defective.
codes.definition: What the cardholder received did not match the merchant's description, or arrived damaged/defective/not fit for purpose, and the merchant would not put it right.
applies_when: Item differs materially from the listing/description
Goods arrived damaged or stopped working within a reasonable time
Counterfeit or misrepresented quality/quantity
does_not_apply_when: Nothing was received at all - use 13.1
Cardholder simply changed their mind - subject to merchant return policy
Deliberate misrepresentation of the whole deal - consider 13.5
required_evidence: Photos or expert report of the defect / mismatch
Evidence the merchant was given a chance to remedy and refused
resolution_steps: Document the discrepancy between what was described and what was received.
Confirm the cardholder contacted the merchant and the merchant did not resolve it.
Check whether the goods were returned or the merchant asked for return.
Raise 13.3 with the description and defect evidence.
Weigh merchant proof that the item matched the description or that the cardholder refused a reasonable remedy.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the item matched the description, passed inspection, or that a repair/replacement/refund was offered and refused
codes.prevention: Use accurate listings and photos; quality-check despatch; operate a clear returns/repair process.

codes.label: Misrepresentation
codes.summary: Cardholder was misled about the terms of the purchase itself.
codes.definition: The merchant materially misrepresented the terms of sale - e.g. a 'free' trial that auto-billed, undisclosed conditions, or a purchase that was not what was promised at the point of agreement.
applies_when: Terms actually applied differ from those presented at purchase
Undisclosed recurring billing after a 'free' or discounted trial
Cardholder agreed based on claims the merchant did not honour
does_not_apply_when: The goods are merely defective / not as described - use 13.3
A cancellation was ignored - use 13.2
Nothing received - use 13.1
required_evidence: Advertising / checkout screenshots showing the represented terms
Cardholder statement of what they were told
resolution_steps: Capture the terms as presented at the time of purchase.
Compare with the terms actually applied / billed.
Raise 13.5 (Misrepresentation) with both.
Where trial-to-paid conversion is involved, check disclosure prominence and consent.
Assess merchant evidence of clear, accepted disclosure.
merchant_remedy: Checkout flow / T&Cs evidence showing the disputed term was clearly disclosed and affirmatively accepted
codes.prevention: Disclose all material terms at the point of consent; make recurring billing and trial conversions explicit and opt-in.

codes.label: Credit Not Processed
codes.summary: Merchant agreed a refund / credit but never processed it.
codes.definition: The merchant issued a credit voucher or agreed a refund (or accepted a cancellation/return) but the credit was not applied to the cardholder's account within a reasonable period.
applies_when: Merchant confirmed a refund or credit in writing
Return accepted or goods sent back, no refund followed
Credit voucher issued but never cleared
does_not_apply_when: No refund was ever agreed - use the code for the underlying problem (13.1 / 13.3)
Goods not received and no refund promised - use 13.1
required_evidence: Refund/credit confirmation or returns acceptance from the merchant
Proof of return (tracking) if goods were sent back
resolution_steps: Obtain the merchant's written agreement to refund / accept the return.
Confirm the reasonable processing period (typically up to ~15-30 days) has passed with no credit.
Raise 13.6 (Credit Not Processed) for the agreed amount.
Match any later merchant credit and withdraw the dispute if fully refunded.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the credit was processed (ARN of the refund) or that no refund was ever agreed
codes.prevention: Process refunds promptly to the original card; send refund confirmations with an ARN; track return receipts.

codes.label: Cancelled Merchandise/Services
codes.summary: Cardholder cancelled a one-off order / booking per policy and was still charged (or not refunded).
codes.definition: The cardholder cancelled merchandise or services (a booking, an order, a contract) in line with the merchant's cancellation policy, but the charge stood or the due refund was not given.
applies_when: Cancellation made within the policy window
Timeshare / booking / event cancelled per terms
Merchant did not refund a validly cancelled order
does_not_apply_when: It is a recurring subscription - use 13.2
Cancellation was outside the policy / after the cut-off
A refund was agreed then not paid - use 13.6
required_evidence: The cancellation policy in force at purchase
resolution_steps: Establish the cancellation terms that applied at the time of purchase.
Confirm the cardholder cancelled within those terms and holds confirmation.
Raise 13.7 for the amount that should not have been charged / should have been refunded.
Assess merchant evidence that cancellation was late or outside policy.
merchant_remedy: Cancellation policy plus evidence the cancellation was outside the permitted window or not made
codes.prevention: Publish cancellation terms clearly; timestamp cancellation requests; auto-refund validly cancelled bookings.

codes.label: Authorization-Related Chargeback
codes.summary: Transaction not properly authorised - no approval, declined, or expired authorization.
codes.definition: Covers authorization failures: required authorization was not obtained, was declined, the approval had expired, or the account was not authorised for the amount cleared.
applies_when: No authorization record for a transaction that required one
Authorization was declined but the sale was completed
Authorization obtained but expired before clearing
Cleared amount exceeds the approved amount beyond tolerance
Account number was invalid / not on file (MA-4812 is being consolidated into this code)
does_not_apply_when: Cardholder denies the transaction as fraud - use MA-4837 / MA-4863
Amount simply keyed wrong at POS - use MA-4831
resolution_steps: Search authorizations for the PAN / amount / date.
Classify the failure: none, declined, expired, amount-exceeded, or invalid/not-on-file PAN.
Confirm the transaction required authorization (above floor / card-not-present / chip).
Raise MA-4808 with the authorization evidence.
Accept representment only with a valid, in-date approval covering the cleared amount.
merchant_remedy: Valid authorization approval code, obtained in time, for the full cleared amount
codes.prevention: Authorize every transaction; settle before approvals expire; block settlement of declines.

codes.label: Account Number Not on File (BEING CONSOLIDATED INTO MA-4808)
codes.deprecated_note: Mastercard is consolidating this code into MA-4808 (Authorization-Related Chargeback) - new guidance says not to use 4812. Kept in this KB only because the ML classifier and SLM in this project were trained before the consolidation and may still emit MA-4812 - treat any such result as MA-4808 going forward, and route new training data to MA-4808 instead.
codes.summary: BEING RETIRED - transaction cleared on an account number the issuer has no record of. Use MA-4808 instead.
codes.definition: The account number in the transaction does not exist on the issuer's file / was never a valid Mastercard account, so it cannot legitimately have been charged. Mastercard is folding this scenario into MA-4808 rather than keeping it as a standalone code.
applies_when: Issuer cannot match the PAN to any account
Key-entry or generation error produced a non-existent PAN
Authorization was not obtained (a valid auth would have rejected the PAN)
does_not_apply_when: The account exists but the cardholder disputes the purchase - use a dispute or fraud code
Wrong-but-valid account of another customer - closer to MA-4831 / processing error
Current Mastercard guidance: use MA-4808, not 4812
required_evidence: Issuer confirmation the PAN is not on file
Clearing record showing the PAN used
resolution_steps: Confirm the PAN does not correspond to any issued account.
Check no authorization approval exists (it could not, for an invalid PAN).
Raise MA-4808 (Authorization-Related Chargeback) - Mastercard no longer wants this filed as a standalone 4812.
Refer to the acquirer for merchant capture remediation.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of a valid authorization approval for that exact PAN
codes.prevention: Never hand-key or 'reconstruct' PANs; require authorization; use chip/contactless/token capture.

codes.label: Transaction Amount Differs
codes.summary: Amount charged is not the amount the cardholder agreed.
codes.definition: The cleared transaction amount differs from the amount the cardholder agreed to at the point of interaction (keying error, wrong tip, altered amount, partial delivery mismatch).
applies_when: Statement amount != receipt / agreed amount
Tip or gratuity added or altered without agreement
Amount changed after the cardholder approved it
does_not_apply_when: Currency is the issue - use MA-4846
It is a duplicate - use MA-4834
Authorization problem - use MA-4808
required_evidence: Receipt / order confirmation with the agreed amount
Statement entry with the cleared amount
resolution_steps: Obtain the agreed amount from the receipt or order confirmation.
Compare with the settled amount and quantify the difference.
Raise MA-4831 for the difference (or full amount if the correct figure cannot be established).
Have the merchant refund the excess; represent only with signed authority for the higher amount.
merchant_remedy: Cardholder-signed receipt or e-authority showing the exact amount cleared was approved
codes.prevention: Confirm final amounts before capture; control tip-adjust windows; reconcile authorised vs settled amounts.

codes.label: Duplicate Processing / Paid by Other Means
codes.summary: One purchase charged more than once, or already paid another way.
codes.definition: A single transaction was submitted multiple times, or the cardholder already paid for the same goods/services by another method.
applies_when: Two or more identical charges (merchant, amount, ~date)
Cardholder holds proof of payment by cash / cheque / other card
does_not_apply_when: Charges relate to genuinely different purchases
Amount differs due to extra legitimate items - use MA-4831
required_evidence: Proof of the alternative payment (receipt, other statement)
resolution_steps: Identify the duplicate entries or alternative-payment proof.
Confirm they cover one and the same purchase.
Raise MA-4834 for the surplus charge.
Reject representment unless the merchant proves distinct goods/services for each charge.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of separate orders / fulfilments, or that the other payment was refunded
codes.prevention: De-duplicate on order ID; void failed captures instead of re-running; reconcile split-tender sales.

codes.label: No Cardholder Authorization
codes.summary: Cardholder states they did not authorise and did not participate in the transaction.
codes.definition: A fraud chargeback where the cardholder confirms they neither made nor authorised the transaction and it was not a family/household member acting for them.
applies_when: Cardholder firmly states they did not make or authorise the transaction, or that they have never used/heard of the merchant (this is the default fraud code for a plain 'this was not me / I never authorised anyone' claim - a signed declaration is evidence to gather, not a precondition for choosing the code)
Card-absent or card-present transaction denied outright
No 3-D Secure / CVM protection shifting liability to the issuer
does_not_apply_when: Cardholder recognises the merchant but disputes goods/service - use MA-4853/4855/4841
Cardholder only says they don't recognise a descriptor / are unsure, without denying it outright - MA-4863
Chip/PIN mechanics central - MA-4870 / MA-4871
resolution_steps: Obtain the cardholder's fraud declaration.
Check for 3-D Secure or PIN that would move liability to the issuer.
Screen for friendly fraud (prior orders, device, delivery address).
Raise MA-4837 with the declaration and authorization data.
Assess merchant compelling evidence before pre-arbitration.
merchant_remedy: 3-D Secure authentication, PIN verification, or compelling evidence linking the cardholder to the purchase
codes.prevention: Enforce 3-D Secure and CVV on card-absent sales; strong CVM on card-present; fraud-screen high-risk orders.

codes.label: Fraudulent Processing of Transactions
codes.summary: Multiple fraudulent transactions by the same merchant on the account.
codes.definition: The account was subjected to more than one fraudulent transaction at the same merchant, indicating merchant-side fraudulent processing rather than an isolated event.
applies_when: Several fraudulent transactions at one merchant within a short period
Pattern suggests merchant compromise or complicity
does_not_apply_when: Single unauthorised transaction - use MA-4837
Cardholder-vs-merchant service dispute - use a 48xx dispute code
required_evidence: List of the related fraudulent transactions
resolution_steps: Compile all related fraudulent transactions at the merchant.
Confirm cardholder denies all of them.
Raise MA-4840 for the set.
Refer the merchant to acquirer risk / Mastercard fraud programmes.
merchant_remedy: Evidence each transaction was legitimately authorised and delivered to the cardholder
codes.prevention: Monitor per-merchant fraud ratios; block compromised merchants; escalate to network fraud programmes.

codes.label: Cancelled Recurring or Digital Goods Transaction
codes.summary: Recurring / subscription / digital-goods charge after cancellation, or a runaway digital-goods purchase.
codes.definition: The merchant billed a recurring transaction after cancellation, or a digital-goods transaction occurred without the required purchase controls / after the cardholder cancelled.
applies_when: Subscription cancelled before the billing date, still charged
Cardholder revoked the continuous authority
Digital goods billed without required spend controls / after cancellation
does_not_apply_when: One-off physical purchase - use MA-4855 / MA-4853
Cardholder simply forgot to cancel - not a valid dispute
Free-trial misrepresentation - consider MA-4853 / 4854
required_evidence: Proof and date of cancellation with confirmation reference
resolution_steps: Get the cancellation proof and confirm its effective date.
Confirm the disputed charge post-dates the cancellation.
Raise MA-4841 for the post-cancellation billing.
Set a stop / block on further authorizations from the merchant.
Review merchant rebuttal for a valid later cancellation date or no cancellation.
merchant_remedy: Evidence no cancellation was received, or it arrived after the billing cycle cut-off; proof of cardholder consent to the charge
codes.prevention: Action cancellations immediately; confirm in writing; support Account Billing Updater and stop instructions.

codes.label: Late Presentment
codes.summary: Transaction submitted for clearing after the permitted window.
codes.definition: The transaction was presented for settlement more than the allowed number of days after the transaction date, and the delay prejudiced the cardholder/issuer (e.g. account since closed).
applies_when: Transaction-date to clearing-date gap exceeds the network limit
Account closed / non-chargeable through normal means because of the delay
does_not_apply_when: Amount / currency / duplicate issues - use MA-4831 / 4846 / 4834
Cardholder disputes the underlying goods - use a 48xx code
required_evidence: Transaction date vs clearing date from settlement data
resolution_steps: Compare transaction date and clearing date.
Confirm the gap exceeds the presentment window.
Raise MA-4842 with both dates.
If the cardholder still accepts the purchase, limit recovery to the loss caused by lateness.
merchant_remedy: Proof the transaction was actually presented within the allowed window
codes.prevention: Settle daily; do not hold transactions; capture at despatch within policy.

codes.label: Correct Transaction Currency Code Not Provided
codes.summary: Wrong currency code cleared, or DCC applied without proper cardholder choice.
codes.definition: The transaction currency code presented does not reflect the currency in which the cardholder transacted, or Dynamic Currency Conversion was applied without a valid, disclosed cardholder election.
applies_when: Billed currency differs from the receipt / agreed currency
DCC applied without the cardholder actively choosing it
Currency code missing or wrong in the clearing record
does_not_apply_when: Only the amount is wrong - use MA-4831
Cardholder just dislikes their bank's FX rate on a correctly-coded foreign purchase
resolution_steps: Compare the agreed currency with the cleared currency code.
If DCC was used, check for evidence of a genuine cardholder choice.
Raise MA-4846 with the receipt and statement.
Seek re-presentment in the correct currency.
merchant_remedy: Terminal log / receipt showing the cardholder chose DCC and the currency code matches
codes.prevention: Default to local-currency billing; make DCC a clear, disclosed cardholder choice; validate currency codes.

codes.label: Questionable Merchant Activity
codes.summary: Transaction identified through a Mastercard merchant-fraud / GMAP / QMAP programme.
codes.definition: The transaction was flagged because the merchant appears in a Mastercard security/questionable-activity programme (e.g. Global Merchant Audit Program), not from an individual cardholder claim.
applies_when: Case cites GMAP / QMAP / merchant-monitoring identification
Merchant breached network fraud/violation thresholds
does_not_apply_when: Ordinary single-transaction fraud - use MA-4837
Service/goods dispute - use a 48xx code
resolution_steps: Confirm the transaction was flagged under a merchant-monitoring programme.
Match it to the reporting period and merchant ID.
Raise MA-4849 - note limited representment rights.
Route to acquirer risk for merchant action.
merchant_remedy: Limited - only where the item was not actually reported or was already credited
codes.prevention: Merchant must remediate the underlying compliance/fraud breach to exit the programme.

codes.label: Installment Billing Dispute
codes.summary: Error in a Mastercard instalment-billing arrangement.
codes.definition: A dispute about an instalment-billing transaction - wrong instalment amount, instalments continuing after payoff/cancellation, or instalment terms not honoured.
applies_when: Transaction was set up as instalments
Instalment amount / count / schedule is wrong
Instalments continued after early settlement or cancellation
does_not_apply_when: Ordinary recurring subscription - use MA-4841
Simple wrong amount on a one-off sale - use MA-4831
resolution_steps: Obtain the agreed instalment schedule.
Compare with what was actually billed.
Raise MA-4850 for the incorrect instalment amount(s).
Have the merchant correct the schedule and refund overbilled instalments.
merchant_remedy: Signed instalment agreement matching the amounts billed
codes.prevention: Document instalment terms clearly; stop instalments promptly on payoff/cancellation.

codes.label: Defective / Not as Described or Not Performed
codes.summary: Goods/services received but defective, not as described, or services not performed.
codes.definition: The cardholder received goods or services that were defective, materially different from the description, or the contracted services were not carried out.
applies_when: Item defective or materially not as described
Services paid for but not performed to the agreed standard/scope
Merchant would not repair, replace or refund
does_not_apply_when: Nothing received at all - use MA-4855
Recurring charge after cancellation - use MA-4841
Refund promised then not paid - use MA-4860
required_evidence: Description / contract at time of purchase
Evidence of the defect / non-performance (photos, report)
Proof the merchant was contacted and did not resolve it
resolution_steps: Document the gap between what was promised and what was delivered.
Confirm the cardholder gave the merchant a chance to remedy.
Check return status if goods are involved.
Raise MA-4853 with the description and defect evidence.
Assess merchant proof of conformity or of a remedy offered and refused.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the goods/services conformed, passed inspection, or a remedy was offered and unreasonably refused
codes.prevention: Accurate descriptions; QA on despatch; documented remediation process.

codes.label: Cardholder Dispute - Not Elsewhere Classified
codes.summary: Legitimate cardholder-vs-merchant dispute that does not fit any other specific code.
codes.definition: A catch-all cardholder dispute (often tied to local consumer-protection law) where the cardholder has a valid claim against the merchant that no other reason code covers.
applies_when: Genuine dispute with a good-faith merchant-resolution attempt
No other 48xx code fits the facts
Often supported by local consumer law
does_not_apply_when: A specific code clearly applies - use that instead
The dispute is really fraud - use MA-4837 / 4863
required_evidence: Full cardholder statement of the dispute
resolution_steps: Confirm no specific reason code fits.
Verify the cardholder attempted to resolve with the merchant.
Document the claim and its basis.
Raise MA-4854 (NEC) with the narrative and evidence.
Be prepared to justify why a specific code did not apply if challenged.
merchant_remedy: Evidence rebutting the specific claim made by the cardholder
codes.prevention: N/A - residual category; monitor for clusters that suggest a systemic merchant issue.

codes.label: Goods or Services Not Provided
codes.summary: Cardholder paid but the goods or services were never provided.
codes.definition: The cardholder was billed for merchandise or services that were not received / not rendered by the agreed date, including merchant closure before fulfilment.
applies_when: Agreed delivery / service date passed with nothing provided
Merchant ceased trading before delivering
Event / booking cancelled by the merchant with no alternative or refund
does_not_apply_when: Goods received but defective / not as described - use MA-4853
Cardholder cancelled - use MA-4841 (recurring) or MA-4853 facts
Refund agreed then not processed - use MA-4860

Cardholder claims the transaction itself is unauthorised/fraudulent (they never made it, don't know the merchant) rather than disputing a real purchase they placed - that is fraud, use MA-4837 / MA-4863, not a goods-not-provided dispute
resolution_steps: Confirm the agreed delivery / performance date has passed.
Check the cardholder contacted the merchant.
Confirm the merchant holds no proof of delivery / performance.
Raise MA-4855 with the order confirmation and contact evidence.
Assess any merchant delivery / performance proof before accepting representment.
merchant_remedy: Proof of delivery / collection to the cardholder, or evidence services were performed
codes.prevention: Realistic fulfilment dates; tracked delivery; proactive refunds on undeliverable orders.

codes.label: Addendum / No-Show
codes.summary: Disputed add-on charge (e.g. hotel/car damage, minibar) or an incorrect no-show charge.
codes.definition: An 'addendum' charge added after the original transaction (incidental charges, damage, fuel, minibar) that the cardholder disputes, or a no-show charge that was applied incorrectly.
applies_when: A separate later charge for incidentals / damage the cardholder did not agree
No-show charge applied despite a valid cancellation or actual use
Add-on amount not substantiated
does_not_apply_when: The whole stay/rental is disputed as not provided - use MA-4855
Amount of the main charge is wrong - use MA-4831
required_evidence: Cancellation confirmation or proof of attendance / return in good condition
resolution_steps: Separate the addendum / no-show charge from the original transaction.
Ask the merchant to substantiate the extra charge (damage report, incidental folio).
If unsubstantiated or a valid cancellation exists, raise MA-4859.
Refund the addendum amount; keep the valid original charge intact.
merchant_remedy: Itemised folio / damage report signed or acknowledged by the cardholder; proof of no valid cancellation
codes.prevention: Disclose incidental-charge policy at check-in; document damage with photos and cardholder acknowledgement.

codes.label: Credit Not Processed
codes.summary: Merchant agreed a refund or accepted a return but never credited the account.
codes.definition: The merchant issued a credit voucher, agreed a refund, or accepted a cancellation/return, but the credit was not applied within a reasonable time.
applies_when: Written refund / credit confirmation from the merchant
Return accepted or goods returned, no credit followed
Credit voucher issued but never posted
does_not_apply_when: No refund was ever agreed - use the underlying code (MA-4853 / MA-4855)
Partial refund dispute where the amount itself is contested - document carefully
required_evidence: Return tracking if goods sent back
resolution_steps: Obtain the merchant's agreement to refund / accept the return.
Confirm the reasonable processing window has passed with no credit.
Raise MA-4860 for the agreed amount.
Withdraw if the merchant subsequently credits in full (match the refund ARN).
merchant_remedy: Proof the credit was processed (refund ARN) or that no refund was agreed
codes.prevention: Refund promptly to the original card; issue refund confirmations with ARNs; track return receipts.

codes.label: Cardholder Does Not Recognize
codes.summary: Cardholder does not recognise the transaction (pre-fraud-confirmation).
codes.definition: An early-stage fraud chargeback where the cardholder does not recognise the transaction; used before a full 'no authorization' fraud confirmation and often resolved by a clearer merchant descriptor.
applies_when: Cardholder says 'I don't recognise this' rather than a firm fraud denial
Merchant descriptor is vague / unfamiliar
No fraud declaration yet completed
does_not_apply_when: Cardholder firmly denies and signs a fraud statement - use MA-4837
Cardholder recognises the merchant but disputes the goods - use a 48xx code
Chip/PIN liability shift central - MA-4870 / 4871
resolution_steps: Provide the cardholder with the full merchant descriptor and location to jog recognition.
If still unrecognised, raise MA-4863.
If the cardholder later confirms outright fraud, move to MA-4837.
Check for friendly-fraud signals before pre-arbitration.
merchant_remedy: Clarified descriptor plus transaction detail (items, delivery, login) linking the cardholder to the purchase
codes.prevention: Use clear, recognisable billing descriptors (trading name + city + support contact).

codes.label: Chip Liability Shift
codes.summary: Counterfeit-card fraud at a non-chip terminal where liability shifts to the acquirer.
codes.definition: Card-present counterfeit fraud where the transaction was not completed as a chip transaction at a chip-capable environment, shifting liability to the acquirer/merchant.
applies_when: Card-present, cardholder denies
Counterfeit card
Chip not read (swiped / keyed) at a chip-capable point or acquirer not chip-enabled
does_not_apply_when: Lost/stolen genuine card with PIN failure - use MA-4871
Card-absent fraud - use MA-4837
Cardholder merely does not recognise - MA-4863
required_evidence: Confirmation the genuine card was retained
resolution_steps: Confirm card-present counterfeit fraud.
Check the POS entry mode - was a full chip read done?
If not, and the environment was chip-capable, raise MA-4870.
Attach entry-mode evidence; reject rebuttals lacking chip/cryptogram proof.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of a successful chip read (cryptogram, TVR/TSI) or that the acquirer/terminal was not chip-capable through no merchant fault
codes.prevention: Chip-first acceptance; disable magstripe fallback; keep terminals EMV-certified.

codes.label: Chip / PIN Liability Shift
codes.summary: Lost/stolen genuine card used without PIN at a PIN-capable environment.
codes.definition: Card-present fraud with a genuine lost/stolen/never-received card where PIN was the expected CVM but was not performed, shifting liability to the acquirer/merchant.
applies_when: Genuine card, reported lost / stolen / not received
Card-present transaction
PIN expected but not captured at a PIN-capable point
does_not_apply_when: Counterfeit card - use MA-4870
Card-absent - use MA-4837
PIN was correctly performed - liability likely stays with issuer
resolution_steps: Confirm the card was genuine but lost/stolen and the sale was card-present.
Check the CVM - was PIN required and performed?
If PIN was expected but absent at a PIN-capable point, raise MA-4871.
Attach the lost/stolen report and CVM evidence.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of successful online/offline PIN verification
codes.prevention: PIN-capable terminals; enforce card-preferred CVM; no signature fallback for PIN-preferring cards.

codes.label: Domestic Chargeback Dispute
codes.summary: Chargeback raised under a domestic (in-country) scheme rule rather than the global Mastercard rules.
codes.definition: Used where a domestic switch / country rulebook defines a chargeback right that does not map to a standard global reason code.
applies_when: Transaction and dispute are domestic and a local rule applies
The local rulebook grants a right not covered by global codes
does_not_apply_when: A standard global code fits - use that
Cross-border transaction - domestic rules generally do not apply
required_evidence: Reference to the specific domestic rule
resolution_steps: Confirm the transaction is domestic and identify the local rule relied on.
Check no global code covers the same facts.
Raise MA-4999 citing the domestic rule.
Follow the domestic scheme's evidence and timing requirements (which may differ).
merchant_remedy: Rebuttal evidence as defined by the applicable domestic rulebook
codes.prevention: Domestic-scheme specific - follow local acquirer guidance.

codes.label: Charge Amount Exceeds Authorization Amount
codes.summary: Charge submitted for more than the amount that was authorised.
codes.definition: The settled charge is greater than the amount Amex approved in authorization, beyond any permitted tolerance.
applies_when: Settled amount > authorised amount
Notification / receipt shows the lower authorised figure
No incremental authorization covers the difference
does_not_apply_when: No authorization at all - use AM-A02
Authorization expired before capture - use AM-A08
Amount keyed wrong with no auth mismatch - use AM-P05
required_evidence: Authorization record with the approved amount
Clearing record with the settled amount
Receipt / confirmation of the agreed figure
resolution_steps: Retrieve the authorised amount and the settled amount.
Confirm the settled amount exceeds the approved amount beyond tolerance and no incremental auth exists.
Raise AM-A01 for the excess.
Have the merchant refund the difference; represent only with an incremental authorization or signed authority.
merchant_remedy: Incremental / secondary authorization covering the excess, or cardholder-signed authority for the final amount
codes.prevention: Obtain incremental authorizations for tips / add-ons; reconcile authorised vs settled before submission.

codes.label: No Valid Authorization
codes.summary: Charge submitted with no valid authorization on record.
codes.definition: The transaction was submitted for payment without a valid Amex authorization approval, or the approval was invalid for the transaction as cleared.
applies_when: No approval code on record
Authorization was declined but the charge was submitted
Approval does not match the transaction (account, amount, date)
does_not_apply_when: Approval exists but the charge exceeds it - use AM-A01
Approval expired before capture - use AM-A08
resolution_steps: Search Amex authorizations for the account / amount / date.
Confirm no valid approval covers the cleared transaction.
Raise AM-A02 (No Valid Authorization).
Accept representment only with a valid, matching approval code.
merchant_remedy: Valid authorization approval matching the account, amount and date of the charge
codes.prevention: Authorize every charge; block submission of declined or unauthorised transactions.

codes.label: Authorization Approval Expired
codes.summary: Charge submitted after the authorization approval had already expired.
codes.definition: A valid approval was obtained but the charge was not submitted for settlement within the approval's validity period, so the approval had lapsed by capture.
applies_when: Approval exists but capture is well after it (e.g. days/weeks later)
No fresh authorization obtained before delayed capture
does_not_apply_when: No approval at all - use AM-A02
Charge exceeds the approved amount - use AM-A01
resolution_steps: Compare the approval timestamp with the settlement date.
Confirm the gap exceeds the approval validity window and no re-auth was done.
Raise AM-A08 (Authorization Approval Expired).
Require a fresh valid authorization for any representment.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of a re-authorization obtained before the delayed capture
codes.prevention: Authorize at (or re-authorize near) the point of shipment/capture; do not rely on stale approvals.

codes.label: Credit Not Processed
codes.summary: Merchant agreed a credit / refund that was never posted.
codes.definition: The merchant issued a credit advice, agreed a refund, or accepted a return/cancellation, but the credit was not applied to the Card Member's account within a reasonable period.
applies_when: Written refund / credit confirmation from the merchant
Return accepted or goods returned, no credit followed
Credit note issued but not posted
does_not_apply_when: Goods were never received and no refund was agreed - use AM-C08
Goods returned/refused without a prior refund agreement - use AM-C04
Recurring billing after cancellation - use AM-C28
resolution_steps: Obtain the merchant's written agreement to credit / accept the return.
Confirm a reasonable period has elapsed with no credit posted.
Raise AM-C02 (Credit Not Processed) for the agreed amount.
Match any later merchant credit and close if fully refunded.
merchant_remedy: Proof the credit was processed (credit reference / date) or that no refund was ever agreed
codes.prevention: Process credits promptly to the Amex account; send credit confirmations; reconcile returns to refunds.

codes.label: Goods / Services Returned or Refused
codes.summary: Card Member returned the goods or refused delivery and has not been refunded.
codes.definition: The Card Member returned the merchandise (or validly refused it at delivery) in line with the merchant's policy and no credit has been received.
applies_when: Goods physically returned with proof (tracking / receipt)
Delivery refused per policy
No refund after a valid return
does_not_apply_when: Merchant explicitly agreed a refund already - use AM-C02
Goods never arrived - use AM-C08
Goods kept but defective - use AM-C31
required_evidence: Proof of return / refusal (carrier tracking, return receipt)
resolution_steps: Confirm the goods were returned or refused within the merchant's policy.
Obtain proof of return delivery back to the merchant.
Raise AM-C04 for the unrefunded amount.
Assess merchant evidence that the return was outside policy or never received.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the return was outside the policy window, incomplete, or not received; or that a refund was issued
codes.prevention: Clear return policy; acknowledge returns on receipt; refund promptly once goods are back.

codes.label: Goods / Services Cancelled
codes.summary: Card Member cancelled the order / booking before delivery and was still charged.
codes.definition: The Card Member cancelled the purchase of goods or services (a one-off order, booking or contract) before fulfilment, consistent with the cancellation terms, but the charge stands or was not refunded.
applies_when: Cancellation made before delivery / service date
Cancellation within the merchant's stated terms
Merchant did not refund the cancelled order
does_not_apply_when: Recurring / subscription billing - use AM-C28
Goods already received - use AM-C04 (returned) or AM-C31 (defective)
Refund was agreed then not paid - use AM-C02
required_evidence: Cancellation terms at time of purchase
Date / method of cancellation and confirmation reference
resolution_steps: Establish the cancellation terms that applied.
Confirm the Card Member cancelled within them and holds confirmation.
Raise AM-C05 (Goods / Services Cancelled).
Assess merchant evidence that cancellation was late or never made.
merchant_remedy: Cancellation policy plus evidence the cancellation was outside the window or not received; proof of delivery before any cancellation
codes.prevention: Publish cancellation terms; timestamp cancellation requests; auto-refund validly cancelled orders.

codes.label: Goods / Services Not Received
codes.summary: Card Member was billed but never received the goods or services.
codes.definition: The Card Member paid for merchandise or services that were not received or not rendered by the agreed date, including cases where the merchant ceased trading before delivery.
applies_when: Agreed delivery / performance date passed with nothing received
Merchant unreachable or closed before fulfilling
Goods indefinitely 'in transit' beyond the promised date
does_not_apply_when: Goods received but defective / not as described - use AM-C31
Card Member cancelled the order - use AM-C05
A promised refund was not paid - use AM-C02
Goods returned and not refunded - use AM-C04
required_evidence: Order confirmation with the expected delivery / service date
Evidence the Card Member contacted the merchant
resolution_steps: Confirm the agreed delivery / performance date has passed with nothing received.
Check the Card Member tried to resolve with the merchant.
Confirm the merchant holds no valid proof of delivery / performance.
Raise AM-C08 (Goods / Services Not Received) with the order confirmation and contact evidence.
Review any merchant delivery proof (tracking to the Card Member's address, signed receipt) before accepting representment.
merchant_remedy: Signed proof of delivery / collection, tracking to the Card Member address, or evidence services were performed
codes.prevention: Realistic delivery dates; tracked, signed delivery for higher value; proactively refund undeliverable orders.

codes.label: Paid by Other Means
codes.summary: Card Member already paid for this purchase by another method.
codes.definition: The same goods or services were paid for by another means (cash, cheque, another card, bank transfer) and the Amex charge is an additional, unowed payment.
applies_when: Card Member holds proof of payment by another method for the same purchase
Amex charge duplicates a payment already made
does_not_apply_when: Two Amex charges for one purchase - use AM-P08 (Duplicate Charge)
Different purchases that look similar
required_evidence: Proof of the alternative payment (receipt, other card statement, bank record)
Link showing both cover the same purchase
resolution_steps: Obtain proof of the alternative payment and match it to the same purchase.
Confirm the Amex charge is additional and unowed.
Raise AM-C14 (Paid by Other Means).
Reject representment unless the merchant shows the other payment was refunded or covered something else.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the other payment was reversed / refunded, or was for a different purchase
codes.prevention: Reconcile multi-tender transactions; void the card charge when the customer switches payment method.

codes.label: No Show or CARDeposit Cancelled
codes.summary: No-show / CARDeposit charge applied despite a valid cancellation or actual use.
codes.definition: A lodging / reservation 'no-show' or CARDeposit charge was billed even though the Card Member cancelled within the allowed period or honoured the reservation.
applies_when: No-show charge despite a cancellation within the permitted window
CARDeposit / advance-deposit charge after a valid cancellation
Card Member actually stayed / used the service but was also no-showed
does_not_apply_when: Cancellation was outside the hotel's stated window
The dispute is about the room/service quality - use AM-C31
General order cancellation - use AM-C05
resolution_steps: Obtain the cancellation policy and the cancellation confirmation.
Confirm the cancellation was within the permitted window.
Raise AM-C18 (No Show / CARDeposit Cancelled).
Assess merchant evidence that the cancellation was late or absent.
merchant_remedy: Reservation terms plus evidence the cancellation was outside the window or never made
codes.prevention: Issue cancellation numbers; honour the stated cancellation window; reconcile no-show billing against the PMS.

codes.label: Cancelled Recurring Billing
codes.summary: Recurring / subscription charge continued after the Card Member cancelled.
codes.definition: The merchant billed a recurring charge after the Card Member cancelled the arrangement or withdrew the continuing authority.
applies_when: Subscription / membership cancelled before the billing date
Continuing authority revoked in writing
Charge dated after a valid cancellation
does_not_apply_when: One-off order cancelled - use AM-C05
Card Member never cancelled
Free-trial misrepresentation - consider AM-C31 / dispute facts
required_evidence: Proof and date of cancellation with confirmation reference
resolution_steps: Obtain the cancellation proof and effective date.
Confirm the disputed charge post-dates the cancellation.
Raise AM-C28 (Cancelled Recurring Billing).
Set a block / stop on further authorizations from the merchant.
Review merchant rebuttal for a later or absent cancellation.
merchant_remedy: Evidence no cancellation was received or that it followed the disputed billing cycle
codes.prevention: Action cancellations immediately; confirm in writing; stop billing on revocation of authority.

codes.label: Goods / Services Not as Described or Defective
codes.summary: Goods/services received but not as described or defective.
codes.definition: The Card Member received goods or services that materially differ from the merchant's description or that are defective / not fit for purpose, and the merchant did not resolve it.
applies_when: Item materially different from the listing / description
Defective or damaged on arrival / early failure
Service not to the agreed scope or standard
does_not_apply_when: Nothing received - use AM-C08
Physical damage in transit specifically - use AM-C32
Changed mind / return - use AM-C04
Refund agreed then not paid - use AM-C02
required_evidence: Photos or expert report of the defect / mismatch
Proof the merchant was contacted and did not remedy it
resolution_steps: Document the difference between description and delivery.
Confirm the Card Member gave the merchant a chance to fix it.
Check return status if applicable.
Raise AM-C31 with the description and defect evidence.
Weigh merchant proof of conformity or of a remedy offered and refused.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the item matched the description / passed inspection, or that repair/replacement/refund was offered and refused
codes.prevention: Accurate listings and photos; despatch QA; clear repair/replace/refund process.

codes.label: Goods / Services Damaged
codes.summary: Goods arrived physically damaged.
codes.definition: The merchandise was received damaged (in transit or on delivery) and the merchant has not replaced, repaired or refunded it.
applies_when: Goods visibly damaged on arrival
Packaging / carrier damage reported promptly
Merchant did not resolve after being notified
does_not_apply_when: Item is simply not as described / faulty by design - use AM-C31
Nothing received - use AM-C08
required_evidence: Photos of the damaged item and packaging
Delivery date and date damage reported
resolution_steps: Obtain dated photos of the damage and the packaging.
Confirm the damage was reported to the merchant promptly.
Raise AM-C32 (Goods / Services Damaged).
Assess merchant evidence of safe despatch / a remedy offered.
merchant_remedy: Proof of undamaged despatch and that a replacement / refund was offered and refused
codes.prevention: Protective packaging; carrier insurance; fast replacement on reported transit damage.

codes.label: Missing Imprint
codes.summary: Disputed card-present charge with no card imprint / electronic record of card presence.
codes.definition: A card-present charge is disputed and the merchant cannot produce an imprint or electronic read proving the physical card was present.
applies_when: Card-present charge disputed
No chip/contactless/magstripe read and no manual imprint on file
Cardholder denies the charge
does_not_apply_when: Card-absent transaction - use AM-F29
Signature is the missing element, not the imprint - use AM-F14
required_evidence: Merchant's transaction record (or absence of card-presence proof)
resolution_steps: Request the merchant's proof of card presence (electronic read or imprint).
If none is produced, raise AM-F10 (Missing Imprint).
Do not accept a representment without a valid card-presence record.
merchant_remedy: Electronic chip/contactless/magstripe capture data or a legible manual imprint
codes.prevention: Always capture the card electronically; keep a manual imprinter only as a documented fallback.

codes.label: Missing Signature
codes.summary: Disputed card-present charge with no cardholder signature where one was required.
codes.definition: A card-present charge is disputed and the merchant cannot produce the required cardholder signature (on the receipt or electronically) for a transaction where signature was the CVM.
applies_when: Signature was the required CVM
No signed receipt / e-signature on file
Cardholder denies the charge
does_not_apply_when: Card presence itself is unproven - use AM-F10
PIN or no-CVM transaction - signature not required
Card-absent - use AM-F29
required_evidence: The unsigned receipt / absence of signature record
resolution_steps: Confirm signature was the applicable CVM for the transaction.
Request the signed sales slip from the merchant.
If none is produced, raise AM-F14 (Missing Signature).
Accept representment only with the signed receipt or a valid alternative CVM record.
merchant_remedy: Signed sales receipt, e-signature capture, or proof a different valid CVM (PIN) was used
codes.prevention: Capture signature/e-signature where it is the CVM; retain receipts for the required period.

codes.label: No Card Member Authorization
codes.summary: Card Member denies making or authorising the transaction (full fraud denial).
codes.definition: A fraud dispute where the Card Member confirms they did not make or authorise the transaction and no household member did so on their behalf.
applies_when: Signed Card Member fraud declaration
Transaction not protected by a liability-shifting CVM / 3DS
Card-absent or card-present denied outright
does_not_apply_when: Card Member merely does not recognise it - clarify descriptor first
Recognises merchant, disputes goods - use a C-code
EMV counterfeit central - use AM-F30
Lost/stolen card central - use AM-F31
required_evidence: Merchant descriptor and any delivery detail
resolution_steps: Obtain the Card Member's signed fraud declaration.
Check for any authentication that shifts liability to Amex/issuer.
Screen for friendly fraud (prior orders, device, delivery address).
Raise AM-F24 (No Card Member Authorization).
Assess merchant compelling evidence before further escalation.
merchant_remedy: 3DS authentication, PIN verification, or compelling evidence tying the Card Member to the purchase
codes.prevention: Enforce 3DS / CVV on card-absent; strong CVM card-present; fraud-screen risky orders.

codes.label: Card Not Present
codes.summary: Disputed card-absent (online / phone / mail) transaction the Card Member denies.
codes.definition: A card-absent transaction (e-commerce, MOTO, recurring) is disputed as not made or not authorised by the Card Member, with no authentication shifting liability away from the merchant.
applies_when: Channel is ecommerce / phone_order / mail_order / recurring
Card Member denies the purchase
No successful 3-D Secure protecting the merchant
does_not_apply_when: Card-present dispute - use AM-F10 / AM-F14 / AM-F30 / AM-F31
Card Member recognises the merchant but disputes goods - use a C-code
3DS-authenticated - liability may sit with the issuer
resolution_steps: Confirm the transaction is card-absent and denied.
Check whether 3-D Secure authentication succeeded.
Screen for friendly fraud (order history, device/IP, delivery address).
If the merchant is liable, raise AM-F29 (Card Not Present).
Review merchant compelling evidence (digital delivery, device match, prior use) before escalating.
merchant_remedy: 3-D Secure authentication or compelling evidence: delivery to the Card Member address, device/IP match, account/login history, prior undisputed orders
codes.prevention: Enable 3-D Secure, AVS and CVV2; device fingerprinting and velocity checks on higher-risk orders.

codes.label: EMV Counterfeit
codes.summary: Counterfeit EMV card used card-present where the chip was not properly read.
codes.definition: Card-present counterfeit fraud where a chip-capable transaction was not completed as a full chip read, shifting liability to the merchant/acquirer.
applies_when: Card-present, Card Member denies
Counterfeit / cloned card
Chip not read (swiped / keyed) at a chip-capable point
does_not_apply_when: Genuine lost/stolen card - use AM-F31
Card-absent - use AM-F29
Full chip read with valid cryptogram - liability likely not with merchant
required_evidence: Confirmation the genuine card was retained
resolution_steps: Confirm card-present counterfeit fraud and that the genuine card was not used.
Check the POS entry mode for a full chip read.
If the chip was bypassed at a chip-capable point, raise AM-F30 (EMV Counterfeit).
Attach entry-mode evidence; reject rebuttals without chip/cryptogram proof.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of a successful chip read (cryptogram / TVR-TSI) or that the environment was not chip-capable through no merchant fault
codes.prevention: Chip-first acceptance; disable magstripe fallback; keep terminals EMV-certified.

codes.label: Lost / Stolen / Non-Received Card
codes.summary: Genuine lost / stolen / never-received card used card-present without proper CVM.
codes.definition: Card-present fraud using a genuine card that was lost, stolen or never received, where the expected cardholder-verification method was not performed.
applies_when: Genuine card reported lost / stolen / not received
Card-present transaction
Expected CVM (PIN) not performed at a capable point
does_not_apply_when: Counterfeit card - use AM-F30
Card-absent - use AM-F29
Correct CVM performed - liability likely not with merchant
resolution_steps: Confirm the card was genuine but lost/stolen/non-received and the sale was card-present.
Check whether the expected CVM (PIN) was performed.
If not, at a capable point, raise AM-F31.
Attach the lost/stolen report and CVM evidence.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of successful PIN or other valid CVM verification
codes.prevention: PIN-capable acceptance; enforce card-preferred CVM; no signature fallback for PIN-preferring cards.

codes.label: Credit Processed as Charge
codes.summary: A refund was submitted as a charge, so the account was debited instead of credited.
codes.definition: The merchant processed a transaction in the wrong direction - a credit / refund was submitted as a debit, taking money from the Card Member instead of returning it.
applies_when: A refund the Card Member expected shows as an additional charge
Statement shows a debit where a credit was due
Merchant confirms a processing-direction error
does_not_apply_when: Refund simply never processed at all - use AM-C02
Amount is wrong but direction is right - use AM-P05
Duplicate charge - use AM-P08
required_evidence: Evidence a credit was due (agreement, credit note)
Statement showing the charge posted instead
resolution_steps: Confirm a credit was owed and the Card Member was instead charged.
Quantify the total impact (the wrong charge plus the missing credit).
Raise AM-P03 (Credit Processed as Charge).
Require the merchant to reverse the charge and post the correct credit.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the transaction was correctly a charge, or that the erroneous charge and the correct credit have both been posted
codes.prevention: Validate transaction direction in the gateway; separate refund and sale workflows; reconcile daily.

codes.label: Incorrect Charge Amount
codes.summary: Charge amount posted is not the amount agreed (no authorization-mismatch angle).
codes.definition: The amount charged differs from the amount the Card Member agreed at the point of sale due to a processing / keying error, transposition, or added amount not agreed.
applies_when: Statement amount != receipt / agreed amount
Transposition or keying error
Surcharge / gratuity added without agreement
does_not_apply_when: The excess is specifically over an authorised amount - use AM-A01
Currency is the issue - use AM-P23
Duplicate - use AM-P08
required_evidence: Itemised receipt / order confirmation with the agreed amount
Statement entry with the charged amount
resolution_steps: Obtain the agreed amount and compare with the amount charged.
Quantify the difference.
Raise AM-P05 (Incorrect Charge Amount) for the excess.
Have the merchant refund the difference; represent only with signed authority for the higher figure.
merchant_remedy: Cardholder-signed receipt / e-authority showing the exact amount charged was agreed
codes.prevention: Confirm the final amount before capture; control tip-adjust; reconcile receipts to settlement.

codes.label: Late Submission
codes.summary: Charge submitted for payment well after the transaction date.
codes.definition: The merchant submitted the charge for settlement outside the permitted number of days from the transaction date, and the delay caused or contributed to the dispute.
applies_when: Gap between transaction date and submission/settlement date exceeds the Amex window
Account closed / charge no longer expected because of the delay
does_not_apply_when: Amount / currency / duplicate problems - use AM-P05 / AM-P23 / AM-P08
Authorization expired - use AM-A08
resolution_steps: Compare the transaction date with the submission date.
Confirm the delay exceeds the allowed window.
Raise AM-P07 (Late Submission) with both dates.
If the Card Member still accepts the underlying purchase, limit recovery to loss caused by the delay.
merchant_remedy: Proof the charge was in fact submitted within the permitted window
codes.prevention: Submit charges promptly (daily); capture at shipment within policy; don't hold approvals open.

codes.label: Duplicate Charge
codes.summary: The same transaction was charged to the Amex account more than once.
codes.definition: A single purchase was submitted and posted multiple times to the same Card Member account.
applies_when: Two or more identical charges (merchant, amount, ~date)
Only one purchase was actually made
does_not_apply_when: Paid once on Amex and once by another method - use AM-C14
Charges are for genuinely separate items
Amount differs due to extra legitimate items - use AM-P05
required_evidence: Order confirmation showing a single purchase
resolution_steps: Identify the duplicate entries and confirm a single underlying purchase.
Raise AM-P08 (Duplicate Charge) for the extra posting(s).
Reject representment unless the merchant proves separate goods/services for each charge.
merchant_remedy: Evidence of separate orders / fulfilments for each charge
codes.prevention: De-duplicate on order ID; void failed captures instead of re-submitting; reconcile settlement batches.

codes.label: Non-Matching Card Number
codes.summary: Charge posted to a card number that does not match the card used.
codes.definition: The account number in the submitted charge does not match the account number of the card actually presented / on file, so the wrong Card Member was billed.
applies_when: Charged account number differs from the card the Card Member holds / used
Key-entry or tokenisation error produced a mismatched number
Card Member has no account matching the charge
does_not_apply_when: Card Member recognises the account but disputes the purchase - use a fraud / C-code
Amount is the problem - use AM-P05
required_evidence: The card / account details held by the Card Member
Any merchant receipt showing the entered number
resolution_steps: Confirm the charged account number is not the Card Member's.
Check for a transposition / key-entry error at the merchant.
Raise AM-P22 (Non-Matching Card Number).
Have the merchant reverse and re-submit to the correct account.
merchant_remedy: Evidence the account number charged matches the card actually presented (chip data / tokenisation record / imprint)
codes.prevention: Avoid manual entry; use chip / contactless / tokenised capture; validate card numbers at entry.

codes.label: Currency Discrepancy
codes.summary: Charge cleared in the wrong currency, or DCC applied without a valid cardholder choice.
codes.definition: The transaction currency billed differs from the currency in which the Card Member agreed to transact, or Dynamic Currency Conversion was applied without a proper, disclosed election.
applies_when: Billed currency differs from the receipt / agreed currency
DCC applied without the Card Member actively choosing it
Wrong currency indicator in the submitted charge
does_not_apply_when: Only the amount is wrong - use AM-P05
Card Member simply dislikes the FX rate on a correctly-billed foreign charge
resolution_steps: Compare the agreed currency with the currency charged.
If DCC was used, check for evidence of a genuine, disclosed Card Member choice.
Raise AM-P23 (Currency Discrepancy) with the receipt and statement.
Seek re-submission in the correct currency.
merchant_remedy: Terminal log / receipt showing the Card Member chose DCC and the billed currency matches that choice
codes.prevention: Bill in local currency by default; make DCC a clear, disclosed choice with the rate shown.
